title: Logs Stopped Arriving in Kibana
intro: Kibana shows no logs newer than 03:14 this morning. The log shippers' own logs are full of '403 Forbidden' errors from Elasticsearch.

steps.hint: Yellow isn't red — data is available. So why are writes rejected?

steps.fake_output:
disk.used disk.avail disk.percent node
    476gb       24gb           95 es-node-1
    471gb       29gb           94 es-node-2
    468gb       32gb           94 es-node-3

steps.prompt: At the flood-stage watermark, ES blocks writes to protect itself. Confirm the indices were marked read-only.
Free space by deleting the oldest log indices (older than the 30-day retention policy).
steps.hint: Freeing space is the actual fix; the read-only flag is the symptom.

steps.prompt: Check disk usage again to confirm nodes are back below the watermarks.
steps.fake_output:
disk.used disk.avail disk.percent node
    301gb      199gb           60 es-node-1
    298gb      202gb           59 es-node-2
steps.hint: Recent ES versions remove the read-only block automatically once usage falls back below the high watermark.

resolution: Retention was never enforced, so indices from months ago kept piling up until every node crossed Elasticsearch's 95% flood-stage watermark. ES responded exactly as designed: it marked indices read_only_allow_delete to avoid filling disks completely and corrupting data, which is why shippers got 403s and logs silently stopped. Deleting indices older than the 30-day policy freed ~170GB per node; newer ES versions lift the block automatically once disk drops below the high watermark (older ones need a manual settings update). Permanent fixes: an Index Lifecycle Management policy that deletes indices after 30 days automatically, and an alert on ES disk usage at ~80% — well before the watermarks start changing cluster behavior.
